card.name: Words introducing optional alternatives in dosing
card.fires_on: Small linking or modal words such as may, can, but, or a comma right before an optional or permitted alternative in dosing or administration instructions. It follows a main instruction and leads into 'be given', 'be used' or 'be divided'.

modes.label: Modal may/can
modes.description: The word may or can sits where the text says something is permitted or possible.
modes.example: The rate of infusion<< can>> be escalated at a rate of 1

modes.label: But or comma before an option
modes.description: A conjunction or comma after a standard instruction introduces an alternative or special case.
modes.example: The daily dose is usually given as a single dose<< but>> may be given in divided doses.

modes.label: If desired or preferred
modes.description: The word or comma after a condition like 'if desired' or 'if preferred' leads into an optional choice.
modes.example: If<< desired>>, the daily dose may be divided.

card.writes: It promotes Chinese words meaning 'can' or 'may', which suggests it adds the idea that an option is permitted.
card.plain: It marks the spot in dosing directions where the text is about to say something is allowed or optional.
